content:
anya: brief thread from the follow-up session: can we avoid full tenant partitioning but still give reliable cost attribution for noisy tenants?

mike: short answer: yes if we combine attr-slimming with a smart fanout for a small set of tenants. fewer shards overall, but we keep fidelity where it matters.

tariq: we should be careful about the "smart" part. detection needs to be stable (not flip-floppy) and inexpensive. propose a 5-minute sliding-cardinality+TPS heuristic.

lucy: Also add a safelist for known enterprise customers that require firm billing fidelity regardless of heuristics. ops won't like surprises.

anya: proposal outline:
- gateway keeps a tiny pinned set: [billing.customer_id, billing.key, tenant.id, service.name]
- all other attrs are slimmed (size limit, name normalizing)
- if tenant hits noisy threshold -> fanout write to a dedicated stream for that tenant for N hours
- metrics: track "attribution_loss" and false-neg rate in nightly evals

mike: fanout semantics: writes go to both main stream (slimmed) and tenant stream (full attrs). query layer can prefer tenant stream if present. avoids cross-partition queries for most ops.

tariq: edge case: what if a tenant toggles noisy often? cost could spike. mitigate with cool-down windows and a hard cap on concurrent dedicated streams (eg 30).

lucy: security note: ensure tenant stream KMS keys + IAM are set correctly. Also retention on tenant streams needs review (dedicated streams may need longer retention for billing disputes).

anya: sample gateway config snippet: 
```
eviction:
  pinned: ["billing.customer_id","tenant.id","service.name"]
  max_attrs: 20
  normalize_names: true

fanout:
  noisy_threshold:
    tps: 1000
    unique_attr_growth_per_min: 500
  retention_hours: 72
  cool_down_mins: 30
  max_concurrent_dedicated: 30
```

mike: telemetry plan: generate a synthetic workload with 200 tenants, inject 5 noisy tenants, run the spike to measure write amplification and query latency impact. also compute cost delta per 1k noisy tps.

ingest-bot: created spike task by @anya -> https://phab.redwood/WORK-eviction-fanout-spike-421

anya: owners: mike+tariq implement spike (4d), lucy builds eval dataset and alerting for attribution_loss. i'll update the RFC with this hybrid-fanout approach afterwards.

lucy: will prepare evals and a dashboard that shows attribution_loss by tenant and by time window.

mike: ack, posting progress into this thread. :thumbsup:
